notice: Python and libraries on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with its standard library (email, imaplib, json, secrets, hmac), while the recording ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with ezgmail 2026.4.28, requests 2.34.2 and aiosmtpd 1.4.6, none of which is on this page. No real Gmail account, phone, ntfy server or Twilio account was ever reached. A browser's Python cannot open sockets between programs, run a server in a thread, start another program or set the process time zone, and Python 3.14 added imaplib's idle(), so thirty-six examples are shown as recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run, each with its reason; the other twenty-one examples were run in the browser and checked against their recorded result: they build and take apart messages, count bytes and characters and parse text with the standard library. Programs of the recording used local stand-ins: the real ezgmail and Google library against a replacement of Google's HTTP object whose replies were written for the course (Stand-in for Gmail), a local SMTP server (Stand-in for an SMTP server), a local recorder in place of ntfy (Stand-in for ntfy), a list of messages in place of a mailbox (Stand-in mailbox), and sample data (a forecast, a page of HTML); their output shows what the libraries send and how the program reacts, not what Gmail, a phone company, ntfy or weather.gov answers, and every such example says so. Not executed at all: a Gmail account, a Google Cloud project and the browser authorisation (so the 7-day expiry of a Testing token and what Gmail does with .exe and .zip attachments are read, not run), any connection to Gmail's servers, any text message and any Twilio account, any publication to ntfy.sh, Windows and macOS (the Popen of qBittorrent), the 153 and 67 character segments of long texts, and Python 3.14.7 and later and the final 3.15.0. Recorded results of 13 October 2026 (the shutdown notices, the DNS answers, the DMARC record) are not run again here. The deck, whose text is the Lecture tab, marks slides 5, 6, 8, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 20 and 23 NOT EXECUTED, says on slides 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 18, 19, 20, 22 and 23 that the program shown ran against a local stand-in, and calls slides 4, 14, 16, 19, 20 and 22 Recorded (results of 13 October 2026 that it does not run again). One correction to the Lecture tab: its text for slide 15 says that 13 of the 18 gateway domains had mail exchangers, but the recorded answers show 12, because sms.cricketwireless.net answered only name aliases (CNAME) and no MX record; the research text says 12 of 18.
